claims.text: A hybrid ab initio and machine-learning approach can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed framework would predict free energies and entropy terms using training data generated by ab initio calculations.
The method is intended to treat high-entropy systems in both solid and fluid states.
The proposed temperature domain is 500–2000 K.
The proposed composition domain consists of multicomponent high-entropy systems containing up to five elements.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn relationships between atomic structures and thermodynamic properties.
Learning structure–property relationships enables efficient prediction of free energies and entropy terms.
The proposed method would reduce computational cost by one to two orders of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method would maintain accuracy comparable to TOR-TILD.
Prediction accuracy for high-entropy systems is uncertain.
Large training datasets may be required.
The method is falsified if its predictions deviate from explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics and TOR-TILD results by more than 10% for more than 50% of the tested systems.
